newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar hovering near 123.50 yen in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dollar hovering near 123.50 yen in Tokyo.

text.p: *Dollar had edged up and was hovering near 123.50 yen in Tokyo after short-covering, stop-loss buying and yen sales in cross-trading helped it recoup earlier morning losses.
*Stop-loss buying detected near 123.20, 123.40 and 123.50 yen, with some dealers saying additional stop-loss buying may emerge around 123.80 yen.
*Some buying by securities firms and institutional investors detected, but main activity short-covering from interbank operators who had sold dollars earlier.
*"Although we're unlikely to see any sudden jumps today, the dollar also stubbornly refuses to fall. Expect a slow rise," one trust bank dealer said.

*Some exporter offers expected to emerge as greenback climbs, but no substantial offers detected. Few long positions remain in market after morning's earlier slump, making further rises entirely possible, dealers said.

*Gains made against yen by mark, sterling and Australian dollar also buoying dollar against yen. Sterling supported on buying by Japanese securities firms, while Aussie solid on strong Australian wage data released in morning.
*Dollar slumped against yen, slipping below 123 yen in morning Tokyo on heavy loss-cut selling, mainly by bank operators. Overseas operators may also have taken part.
*Selling emerged once dollar broke below 123.30 yen and then picked up speed as dealers liquidated accumulated long positions.
*Profit-taking sales of marks and pound for yen also weighed on dollar/yen. Sterling sales especially heavy, and it fell to near 201.59/71 yen against 202.71 yen in early trade.
*Mark fell to around 74.72/75 yen from 74.95 yen in early trade.
*But bargain-hunting bids from importers and institutional investors near 122.80 yen halted dollar slide.
*Dollar steady at its New York closing level in early Tokyo trade after paring earlier gains due to profit-taking and caution about recent rapid gains, dealers said.
*But upward momentum expected to continue, with dollar supported at around 123.20 yen, a Japanese bank dealer said.
